premise: Choosing to test his experimental polio vaccine on himself and his own family.
hook: To prove his vaccine was safe, a medical researcher injected the untested formula directly into the arms of his wife and children.
key_facts: Led a research team at the University of Pittsburgh in the early 1950s.
Utilized a 'killed' virus approach rather than a live-attenuated one.
Announced successful nationwide clinical trial results in April 1955.
Declined to patent the polio vaccine, ensuring it remained accessible globally.

premise: Swimming 110 miles from Cuba to Florida at age 64 without a shark cage after decades of failed attempts.
hook: At age 64, after jellyfish stings and asthma attacks stopped her previous tries, she stepped back into shark-infested waters.
key_facts: Attempted the Cuba-to-Florida swim for the first time in 1978 without success.
Resumed long-distance marathon swimming decades later at age 60.
Completed the historic 110-mile crossing from Havana to Key West in 2013.
Spent over 52 hours continuously swimming in open ocean.

premise: A self-taught mathematical prodigy from India who performed complex calculations faster than early computers without any formal education.
hook: She left school at a very young age, yet traveled the world effortlessly outperforming massive electronic mainframes.
key_facts: Born in Bangalore, India, with no formal mathematical training.
Demonstrated her calculation abilities through public roadshows across India from childhood.
Computed the 23rd root of a 201-digit number in 50 seconds at Imperial College London in 1980.
Earned the moniker 'Human Computer' for her exceptional mental arithmetic feats.

premise: A struggling actor who quit Hollywood to work as a professional carpenter until a chance encounter on a casual job changed his life.
hook: He built cabinets for George Lucas's office just to pay the rent, never expecting it would lead to one of cinema's greatest roles.
key_facts: Spent over a decade taking minor television roles while struggling to make a living in Los Angeles.
Taught himself carpentry and built cabinets for prominent directors and studios.
Hired to build a doorway at a casting office where George Lucas was holding auditions.
Cast as Han Solo in Star Wars after initially just reading lines for other actors during auditions.

premise: Emerging from a modest background in southern India to become the country's first chess Grandmaster and multi-time World Champion.
hook: He learned the complex rules of chess from his mother in a quiet suburban home, long before India had any chess infrastructure.
key_facts: Born in Mayiladuthurai, Tamil Nadu, and learned chess at the age of six.
Became India's first Grandmaster in 1988 at the age of 18.
Won the FIDE World Chess Championship multiple times across different formats.
Popularized chess significantly across India, inspiring a new generation of grandmasters.

premise: Deciding to ignore conservative children's book publishing standards to depict raw, scary childhood emotions.
hook: Editors warned him that his monsters were far too terrifying for young readers, but he refused to change a single line.
key_facts: Grew up in New York City with frail health, spending much of his childhood indoors drawing.
Worked as an illustrator before writing and illustrating his own children's books.
Authored and illustrated 'Where the Wild Things Are' in 1963.
The book initially faced controversy for its dark themes before becoming an international classic.

premise: Attempting a grueling 110-mile open-ocean swim from Cuba to Florida at age 64 after multiple prior failures.
hook: Stung by jellyfish and battered by brutal currents, she refused to give up on a lifelong dream that beat her four times before.
key_facts: First attempted the Cuba-to-Florida swim in 1978 without a shark cage and failed.
Resumed training in her sixties after decades away from extreme marathon swimming.
Endured severe box jellyfish stings and asthma attacks during her final attempt.
Successfully completed the continuous swim from Havana to Key West in 2013 at age 64.

premise: A teenage amateur astronomer whose life changed after a prestigious observatory invited him to speak because of a postcard.
hook: A simple postcard he mailed about a celestial observation landed him a mentorship with the director of the Hayden Planetarium.
key_facts: Grew up in New York City and built his own telescope as a high school student.
Photographed the moon and planets from his Bronx apartment rooftop.
Noticed by the director of the Hayden Planetarium after writing about a sky observation.
Went on to earn a PhD in astrophysics and become the director of the same planetarium.
